title: Same structure, two eras: compare the moves before you judge
outcomes: Compares two games of one structure from different eras using facts from the move lists: when each side acted on the base and where the queen went
States a difference in how the structure was handled without calling either era right or wrong
Checks an old annotator's remark against today's engine and says what each source measures
Says when there is no remark to compare, and keeps the source's polemic out of his own text

steps.text: **Two games of one structure, a century apart.** Compare facts first: when did each side act on the base of the pawn chain (the pawn on d4), where did the queen go, did the king castle? Use the move list, and use the engine only for what it measures. Two games are two data points. They show how to compare, not how a whole era played.

steps.caption: 1916: Chajes (White) against Capablanca (Black), up to Black's ninth move.

line.say: White opens with the king's pawn.
White takes the centre with a second pawn.
White's bishop attacks the knight on f6.
Black's bishop attacks the knight on c3.
White advances: the chain d4-e5 forms.
Black attacks the bishop with a pawn.
Black trades his bishop for the knight.
White's queen attacks the pawn on g7.
White's bishop goes back to c1.
Black attacks White's d4 pawn with the c-pawn.

claims.statement: After 5.e5 White's e5 pawn is protected by d4.
After 8.Qg4 one white piece attacks g7.

steps.prompt: Use the 1916 move list you just watched.

steps.caption: 2013: an online five-minute game between two players rated about 2100, up to White's eleventh move.

line.say: White opens with the king's pawn.
White takes the centre with a second pawn.
White advances: the same chain forms.
Black attacks the base at once.
White adds a defender to d4.
White advances a pawn on the kingside.
Black takes the bishop with check.
White's queen recaptures: it leaves d1 at last.

claims.statement: After 3...c5 a black pawn attacks d4.
After 4.c3 two white pieces defend d4.

fields.label: Move at which Black first played ...c5 in the 2013 game
Move at which White's queen first left d1 in the 2013 game
Which comparison stays inside the evidence?
options: In these two games Black's c-pawn first attacked d4 at move 9 in 1916 and at move 3 in 2013, and White's queen left d1 at move 8 and move 11.
In 1916 players did not understand pawn chains.
The 2013 game is better because it is newer.
fields.answer: In these two games Black's c-pawn first attacked d4 at move 9 in 1916 and at move 3 in 2013, and White's queen left d1 at move 8 and move 11.

steps.text: **An old remark and today's number.** An annotator of 1921 had no engine. Today's engine gives a number for concrete play at a fixed depth. The two can agree, differ, or measure different things (a plan against a count). **Rule of thumb:** two moves within 40 centipawns are both fine by the engine; that gap alone does not make an old move wrong. Do not import a source's quarrels.

**What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** The Openings explorer shows how often moves are played today, by rating band, in online games (September 2026): good for what is common now, not for what was common then. The app has no library of historical games yet (planned). Until then, compare two games by hand, as here.

steps.prompt: Write two or three sentences comparing the two games, in your own words. Use only facts from the move lists and one engine fact. Do not say which era was better.
